title: In light models of 15 heads from CT, an eyelid-to-forehead near-infrared channel did not sample clearly more orbitofrontal cortex than a forehead channel of equal length
abstract: At equal optode separation, near-infrared optodes on the upper eyelid did not give a clear gain in sensitivity to the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) over a standard forehead channel. This matters because the OFC is central to reward research, functional MRI loses signal there, forehead near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is often said to measure it, and patents claim that light from the eyelid reaches it. We made light models of 15 adult heads from public head CT and simulated 830 nm light with a Monte Carlo code. The share of a region is the mean path of detected photons in it, divided by their mean path in tissue. A forehead pair 30 mm apart had a median OFC share of 0.55% and a frontopolar-cortex (FP) share of 5.6%. A pair from the upper eyelid to the forehead, also 30 mm, had an OFC share of 0.63% (per-head ratio 1.24, 95% CI 0.70-1.59) and less FP (2.4%), so its OFC/FP ratio was higher in 15/15 heads. Against a vertical pair of the same length that starts at the brow, the eyelid optode gave only 1.16 times (30 mm) and 1.20 times (40 mm) the OFC share. The absolute shares depend on where the OFC border is drawn (0.25-1.05% for the forehead pair). The nearest OFC was 20.9 mm from the eyelid optode and 11.5 mm from the forehead. Light sources on the upper eyelid put no more power into the OFC than a forehead source (0.126% and 0.179% against 0.183%). In an exploratory analysis of photons that arrive 2-3 ns after a light pulse, two eyelid optodes sampled more OFC (3.9%) than FP (3.1%), but a horizontal pair at brow level did as well (3.6% OFC, 1.6% FP). Early light is 340,000 times the late light for the eyelid pair and 1,700 times for the brow pair; with a detector time response that has a slow tail (1% of its area, 0.3 ns), the eyelid pair lost its advantage. Scalp and muscle blood signals were larger than the OFC signal in all pairs. A 1 mm radius source on a closed lid, aimed at the eye, had to stay below 1.8 mW in the worst of 27 eyes (median 4.8 mW) to keep lens and cornea under the ICNIRP infrared limit. The higher OFC/FP ratio held in all 14 robustness tests (other tissue properties, OFC boundaries, scattering model, random seed, model size); the OFC share ratio itself ranged 0.83-1.50. Limits: tissue classes from CT, literature optical properties, ideal optodes; no physiological noise, blinks or eye movements. Forehead fNIRS channels above the brow measure mainly frontopolar cortex, and the eyelid gives little or no extra optical access to the OFC.
